openrouter-glm.gate: separate quota pool (the operator's OpenRouter credit balance) — consumes no Anthropic/xAI/Cursor/Kiro limits
openrouter-glm.note: Transport is a RAW CURL via `or-free.sh --default` — NOT opencode. Investigated 2026-09-03: GLM 5.3 Flash itself is clean (raw API: correct code, `<`/`&&` literal, 3/3, ~$8e-5, <2s round-trip), but `opencode run` is slow (~2 min startup) and INTERMITTENTLY HTML-escapes code output (`<` `>` `&` — forkdeck 2026-09-02, 2 of 3 runs). Use `--code` for code-gen (html.unescape guard). GLM 5.3 Flash (z-ai/Zhipu) is the only model the `default`-workspace guardrail permits (allowlist of one, across Z.AI / Novita / DeepInfra); `openrouter/free` also passes. Every other pinned slug -> `Filter by Guardrails`. Widen at https://openrouter.ai/workspaces/default/guardrails.

model_pin.rule: the guardrail permits only this + openrouter/free; do not pin another slug without confirming the allowlist changed
model_pin.zdr: z-ai is third-party; prompts may be retained. the operator approved private-repo contents (Grimdex + Grimlore) on THIS path 2026-09-02 — a deliberate exception to the standing 'keep private KB off third-party' rule.

openrouter-glm.caveat: Fast reasoner, shallow on deep architecture / adversarial review / nuanced prose — seat on bulk-code/draft/docs/summary behind a review gate, never a finisher on judgment work (grimdex-d030). GLM 5.3 Flash is a REASONING model: it spends completion tokens on hidden reasoning first, so `max_tokens` must be generous (or-free.sh sets 8000) or `content` comes back empty. No routing-ratings.jsonl rows yet — rate early runs.

openrouter-free.gate: OpenRouter 'Free Models Router' (`openrouter/free`) — $0, genuinely free. Consumes no Anthropic/xAI/Cursor/Kiro limits and no OpenRouter credit. the operator added `openrouter/free` to the `default` workspace allowlist alongside GLM 5.3 Flash.
openrouter-free.note: Transport is `or-free.sh --default openrouter/free` (raw curl, ~1s) — switched off `opencode` 2026-09-03 (slow + intermittent HTML-escaping, same as openrouter-glm). `openrouter/free` is a ROUTER — it picks among genuinely-free models per request (seen: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free), so which model answers and the quality vary run to run. Free endpoints are often rate-limited; on 429 or empty content, fall back to `openrouter-glm` (paid GLM 5.3 Flash) or `haiku`. For a SPECIFIC open model rather than the router's pick, drop `--default` to hit the `free-models` workspace ($1/wk cap): deepseek-v3.2-exp / deepseek-chat-v3.1 / deepseek-r1 / glm-4.6 / qwen3-coder / llama-3.3-70b / mistral-small-3.2.

model_pin.rule: the Free Models Router only — never pin a premium slug on this row (the operator: Claude/Grok/Gemini come from their own harness paths; OpenRouter here is the free open set)
model_pin.zdr: Free endpoints are training-permitted third-party. the operator approved private Grimdex + Grimlore contents on the OpenRouter path 2026-09-02 — but prefer `openrouter-glm` for anything sensitive; use this row for generic / scaffolding / high-volume-low-stakes work.

openrouter-free.caveat: Router output varies model to model — never a finisher on judgment work (grimdex-d030); seat on bulk/draft/docs/summary behind a review gate. Expect intermittent 429s from free-tier capacity. No routing-ratings.jsonl rows yet — rate early runs.

planning_consensus.note: BIG planning (new subsystem, cross-cutting change, irreversible call) → run the 3-way panel and synthesize. Minor planning → opus alone, no panel.

policy.late_window_note: On the LAST day of a paid pool's weekly window, spend its high tiers aggressively — unused weekly quota is wasted. Priority order for the burn: code review and planning first (that is where the strong models pay off most), then bulk. Applies to Claude (opus/sonnet subagents) and any other pool with a weekly reset. Pass -LateWindow to Select-FleetWorker; check windows with the quota probe.
